key_insight: Separating permanent parametric representations from transient non-parametric representations helps continual reinforcement learning balance knowledge retention with rapid adaptation.
engineering_relevance: This architecture may inform adaptive engineering control, but the abstract provides no solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling validation.
method: Decompose value estimation into permanent and transient components.
Use parametric representations for long-term generalization.
Introduce a non-parametric transient value approximation for online, situation-specific adaptation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical and empirical investigation, with performance exceeding competitive baselines on image-based tasks and Craftax-Classic.
watch_item: Memory and computational scaling of the non-parametric component require scrutiny; the abstract gives no resource-cost measurements.
paper_title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
